provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Experienced Manager: Investigate a Performance Gap Fairly
prompt: You lead eight analysts. Casey completed 12 of 20 assigned reviews this month; the team median was 18. The assignment sheet has no complexity field. Quality checks found one correction in Casey’s completed work and one in a peer’s, but the sample sizes differ. Your manager asks you to start a formal warning immediately. Explain your next steps to the manager (the AI).

rubric.label: Check comparability
rubric.description: Interprets throughput and quality evidence carefully.

anchors.0: Treats 12 versus 18 as proof of poor effort or converts unequal quality samples into a ranking.
anchors.4: Separates workload mix, availability, quality and individual behavior, states the limits of the current comparison and seeks proportionate job-relevant evidence.

anchors.0: Guarantees a warning or dismissal without inquiry.
anchors.2: Discusses expectations and support with Casey.
anchors.4: Invites Casey’s account, fixes controllable blockers, agrees measurable expectations with a review period and consults the stated procedure before formal action.

anchors.0: Hides the issue or promises that support will necessarily resolve it.
anchors.2: Explains that more evidence is needed.
anchors.4: Gives the manager a dated plan for evidence, support and review; protects confidentiality while keeping the performance concern visible and open to a different conclusion.

reference.scenario: You lead eight analysts. Casey completed 12 of 20 assigned reviews this month; the team median was 18. The assignment sheet has no complexity field. Quality checks found one correction in Casey’s completed work and one in a peer’s, but the sample sizes differ. Your manager asks you to start a formal warning immediately. Explain your next steps to the manager (the AI).

facts.value: Casey handled six escalated cases, while most peers handled one or two. A tooling problem also blocked three assigned cases for two days.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about case mix, obstacles or comparable evidence

facts.value: The organization’s fictional procedure requires consulting People Operations before formal action and documenting expectations and support. No outcome is predetermined.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about process or authority

model_points: Separates workload mix, availability, quality and individual behavior, states the limits of the current comparison and seeks proportionate job-relevant evidence.
Invites Casey’s account, fixes controllable blockers, agrees measurable expectations with a review period and consults the stated procedure before formal action.
Gives the manager a dated plan for evidence, support and review; protects confidentiality while keeping the performance concern visible and open to a different conclusion.

probes.trigger: candidate uses team median as a quota
probes.question: How would the escalated cases affect that comparison?

probes.trigger: candidate rejects any performance concern after hearing about blockers
probes.question: What evidence would still warrant a supported performance conversation?
How will you correct the record and explain the revised plan?

fair_alternatives: A workload adjustment can be an evidence-gathering and support step without assuming there is no performance issue.
Immediate escalation is valid if a separately evidenced safety concern emerges; none is supplied here.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Separate observations from conclusions
learning_drills.prompt: Write a short evidence table: observed fact, possible explanation, missing evidence and next action. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
